name: BG 2.7
lines: yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṁ brūhi tan me
śiṣyas te 'haṁ śādhi māṁ tvāṁ prapannam
translation: My very nature is overcome by the weakness of pity, and my mind is confused about where my duty lies. I am asking You — please tell me clearly what is truly best for me. I am now Your student; I have surrendered to You. Please guide me.

name: BG 2.13
translation: Just as the soul within this body passes through childhood, youth, and old age, so too it passes into another body at death. A person of steady wisdom is not disturbed by this change.

name: BG 2.20
lines: nāyaṁ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ
translation: The soul is never born and never dies; it does not come into being and then cease to exist. It is unborn, eternal, ever-existing, and primordial. It is not killed when the body is killed.

name: BG 2.44
translation: For those whose minds are captivated by such talk, who are attached to sense enjoyment and worldly position, a resolute, one-pointed determination directed toward the Self does not arise.

name: BG 3.27
translation: All actions are, in truth, performed by the modes of material nature. But one whose mind is bewildered by false ego thinks, 'I am the doer.

name: BG 4.2
translation: This knowledge was received in that way, passed down through an unbroken succession, and saintly kings understood it thus. But over the long passage of time, that yoga has become lost, O Parantapa.

name: BG 4.8
translation: To protect the righteous, to destroy the wicked, and to firmly re-establish dharma, I appear age after age.

name: BG 4.9
translation: One who truly understands, in reality, the divine nature of My birth and activities does not, upon leaving this body, take birth again — that person comes to Me, O Arjuna.

name: BG 4.34
translation: Learn that truth by approaching a teacher with humility, by sincere inquiry, and by service. Those who possess knowledge and have seen the truth will impart that knowledge to you.

name: BG 5.22

words.en: born of contact with the senses
having a beginning and an end

translation: Pleasures that arise from contact with the senses are, indeed, sources of suffering — they have a beginning and an end. A wise person, O Kaunteya, does not delight in them.

name: BG 5.29
translation: Knowing Me as the recipient of all sacrifice and austerity, the supreme Lord of all worlds, and the true friend of every living being, one attains peace.

name: BG 6.47
translation: And of all yogīs, the one who worships Me with faith, their inner self absorbed in Me, is considered by Me to be the most perfectly united in yoga.

name: BG 7.5
translation: This is My lower nature. But beyond it, know that I have another, higher nature, O mighty-armed one — the living beings, by whom this whole world is sustained.

name: BG 7.14

words.en: composed of/made from the three modes

translation: This divine energy of Mine, composed of the three modes of nature, is very difficult to overcome. But those who surrender to Me alone cross beyond this māyā.

name: BG 7.19
translation: After many births, the one who has attained true knowledge surrenders to Me, understanding that Vāsudeva is everything. Such a great soul is very rare.

name: BG 8.5
translation: Whoever, at the time of death, leaves the body remembering Me alone attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.

name: BG 8.16

words.en: up to the abode of Brahmā

translation: All the worlds up to the abode of Brahmā are subject to repeated birth and death, O Arjuna. But one who attains Me, O Kaunteya, never takes birth again.

name: BG 9.2
translation: This is the king of all knowledge, the most confidential of secrets, the purest and highest teaching. It is directly realizable, in accord with dharma, joyful to practice, and imperishable.

name: BG 9.4
translation: This entire universe is pervaded by Me in My unmanifest form. All beings rest in Me — yet, in truth, I am not confined within them.

name: BG 9.14
translation: Constantly glorifying Me, striving with firm resolve, bowing down before Me with devotion, they worship Me, ever united in this practice.

name: BG 13.22

words.en: good and bad, high and low

translation: The living being, situated in material nature, experiences the modes born of that nature. Attachment to these modes is the cause of its taking birth in good and bad forms of life.

name: BG 13.23
translation: In this body there is also another, transcendent being — called the witness, the permitter, the sustainer, the supreme enjoyer, the great controller, and the Supreme Soul.

name: BG 14.26
translation: One who serves Me with unwavering devotion transcends these three modes of nature completely and becomes fit for realization of Brahman.

name: BG 15.7

words.en: in the world of living beings
the six, mind being the sixth

translation: The living beings in this world are eternal fragmental parts of Me. Bound in material nature, they struggle hard with the six senses, mind being the sixth.

name: BG 15.15
lines: vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyo
translation: I am seated in the hearts of all beings. From Me come memory, knowledge, and forgetfulness. I alone am that which is to be known through all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of Vedānta and the knower of the Vedas.

name: BG 18.54
translation: One who has realized Brahman becomes joyful in the self; such a person neither grieves nor desires, and, being equal-minded toward all beings, attains supreme devotion to Me.

name: BG 18.55
translation: Only through devotion can one truly know Me — how great I am and what I am in essence. And having known Me in truth, one enters into Me immediately thereafter.

name: BRS 1.1.11
translation: The highest form of devotion is the favorable cultivation of service to Kṛṣṇa — free from any desire other than that service, and unclouded by philosophical speculation or fruitive activity.

name: BRS 1.1.12

words.en: by being fully directed toward Him (the Lord)
of the Lord of the senses (Kṛṣṇa)

translation: Bhakti is service rendered to the Lord of the senses, through one's own senses, when that service is completely free of all material designations and purified by being directed fully toward Him.

name: BRS 1.2.234

words.en: the holy name of Kṛṣṇa and so on (form, qualities, pastimes)

translation: Therefore Kṛṣṇa's holy name and His other transcendental features cannot be perceived by material senses. But that name reveals itself, of its own accord, on the tongue and senses of one inclined toward His service.

name: BRS 1.2.255
translation: When a person, unattached to sense objects, uses them only as appropriate and always in connection with Kṛṣṇa, without becoming entangled — that is called proper renunciation (yukta-vairāgya).

name: ISO Invocation
translation: That (the Supreme) is complete and whole, and this (the manifested universe) is also complete and whole. From that completeness, this completeness has come. Even after this completeness is taken from that completeness, that completeness alone remains.

name: ISO 1

words.en: which is set aside/renounced (as belonging to the Lord)

translation: Everything animate or inanimate within this universe is pervaded by the Lord. One should therefore accept only what is set aside as one's own share, and not covet what belongs to another.

name: NOI 1

words.en: the urge of the belly and genitals
can make disciples (i.e., is fit to teach)

translation: A steady person who can control the urges of speech, mind, anger, tongue, belly, and genitals is qualified to guide others throughout the entire world.

name: NOI 2

words.en: either rigid over-attachment to rules or neglect of them

translation: Devotion is destroyed by these six things: overeating or over-accumulating, excessive unnecessary endeavor, idle talk, rigid or careless attitudes toward rules, association with worldly people, and a restless, greedy mind.

name: NOI 3

words.en: through engaging in various favorable practices
through behavior befitting a devotee/saintly conduct

translation: Devotion is brought to perfection through six things: enthusiasm, firm conviction, patience, engaging in the appropriate practices, giving up unfavorable association, and following in the conduct of the saintly.

name: NOI 4
translation: Giving and accepting gifts, sharing one's inner thoughts in confidence and inquiring after another's, and offering and accepting food — these are the six marks of loving exchange between devotees.
